header.title: SVG Whiteboarding over Shared XML Editing (Extended Profile)
header.abstract: This specification defines an SVG whiteboard as a Jingle application type whose shared document is synchronized with Shared XML Editing (XEP-0284). This is the extended profile: it contains the minimal, standards-only profile plus optional, separately negotiated extensions for capability discovery, image hosting, large attachments and initiation from a chat. It is intended to replace the deprecated, Psi-specific whiteboarding profile that predated XEP-0284.

revision.remark: Initial extended profile: minimal profile plus optional extensions.

section1.p: XEP-0113 defines a minimal, message-based whiteboarding protocol built on a restricted subset of SVG path data. It is stateless and does not provide a shared document model.

XEP-0284 (Shared XML Editing, SXE) instead provides a general mechanism for collaboratively editing an XML document: participants synchronize a set of records that map onto a DOM tree, and XEP-0284 defines Jingle as the session management layer for such sessions. A whiteboard is a natural SXE application: the shared XML document is an SVG document.

This specification defines that application type. It is deliberately minimal: it adds no new XML vocabulary beyond one Jingle application-type namespace, and it defines only the conventions needed to interpret the shared SVG document. Everything else — session management, records, edits, conflict handling — is defined by Jingle (XEP-0166) and Shared XML Editing (XEP-0284).

An earlier whiteboarding profile used by the Psi client relied on a pre-standardization (ProtoXEP) form of SXE with a custom negotiation vocabulary and the namespace http://jabber.org/protocol/sxe. That profile is deprecated. This specification is the standards-based replacement, and Psi is expected to be updated to implement it.

This document is the extended profile. It is a strict superset of the minimal profile: every requirement of the minimal profile applies, and the additional capabilities in Section 12 are optional and individually negotiated. A client implementing only the minimal profile can participate in the same session.

ol.li: Allow freehand drawing and geometric editing on a shared canvas.
Represent the canvas as a self-describing SVG document.
Use existing standards for session management and synchronization, introducing no new synchronization vocabulary.
Require no server modifications beyond those already required by the referenced specifications.

di.dd: The SVG document, rooted at <svg/>, that holds the whiteboard contents and is synchronized by SXE.
An SXE session (XEP-0284) whose Jingle application type is urn:xmpp:jingle:apps:svg-whiteboard:0.
The entity that relays SXE payloads; the session initiator, a Multi-User Chat room, or a dedicated component.
The synchronized state of a single DOM node (defined in XEP-0284).
The record identifier (defined in XEP-0284), distinct from the SVG id attribute.
The drawing area, defined by the viewBox attribute of the root <svg/> element.

section1.p: The whiteboard is identified as a Jingle application type by the namespace urn:xmpp:jingle:apps:svg-whiteboard:0. This namespace is used on the Jingle <description/> element and has no child elements in the minimal profile.
The shared XML document of the session is an SVG document whose root element is <svg/> in the namespace http://www.w3.org/2000/svg. The document conventions are defined in Section 10.

Session management is provided by Jingle (XEP-0166), as required by XEP-0284. The application supplies the <description/> element, and the transport is the SXE Jingle transport urn:xmpp:jingle:transports:sxe, which carries at least one <host/> element.

section2.example: <iq from='kingclaudius@shakespeare.lit/castle' to='laertes@shakespeare.lit/castle' id='jingle1' type='set'> <jingle xmlns='urn:xmpp:jingle:1' action='session-initiate' initiator='kingclaudius@shakespeare.lit/castle' sid='851ba2'> <content creator='initiator' name='whiteboard'> <description xmlns='urn:xmpp:jingle:apps:svg-whiteboard:0'/> <transport xmlns='urn:xmpp:jingle:transports:sxe'> <host>kingclaudius@shakespeare.lit</host> </transport> </content> </jingle> </iq>
section2.p: The responder acknowledges the offer as described in XEP-0166.

section2.example: <iq from='laertes@shakespeare.lit/castle' to='kingclaudius@shakespeare.lit/castle' id='jingle2' type='set'> <jingle xmlns='urn:xmpp:jingle:1' action='session-accept' initiator='kingclaudius@shakespeare.lit/castle' sid='851ba2'> <content creator='initiator' name='whiteboard'> <description xmlns='urn:xmpp:jingle:apps:svg-whiteboard:0'/> <transport xmlns='urn:xmpp:jingle:transports:sxe'> <host>kingclaudius@shakespeare.lit</host> </transport> </content> </jingle> </iq>

section2.p: A session is ended, or an offer refused, with a Jingle session-terminate. A responder that does not support the application type SHOULD use the unsupported-applications reason.
section2.example: <iq from='laertes@shakespeare.lit/castle' to='kingclaudius@shakespeare.lit/castle' id='jingle3' type='set'> <jingle xmlns='urn:xmpp:jingle:1' action='session-terminate' initiator='kingclaudius@shakespeare.lit/castle' sid='851ba2'> <reason> <unsupported-applications/> </reason> </jingle> </iq>

section1.p: An entity that supports this profile MUST advertise, via Service Discovery (XEP-0030), the following features:

ul.li: urn:xmpp:sxe:0 — Shared XML Editing is supported.
urn:xmpp:jingle:transports:sxe — the SXE Jingle transport is supported.
urn:xmpp:jingle:apps:svg-whiteboard:0 — this application type is supported.

section1.p: It SHOULD also expose the shared-editing identity described in XEP-0284 (discovery identity type sxe in the collaboration category).

example.caption: Service discovery response advertising SVG whiteboarding

section1.example: <iq from='kingclaudius@shakespeare.lit/castle' to='laertes@shakespeare.lit/castle' id='disco1' type='result'> <query xmlns='http://jabber.org/protocol/disco#info'> <identity category='collaboration' type='sxe'/> <feature var='urn:xmpp:jingle:1'/> <feature var='urn:xmpp:sxe:0'/> <feature var='urn:xmpp:jingle:transports:sxe'/> <feature var='urn:xmpp:jingle:apps:svg-whiteboard:0'/> </query> </iq>

section1.p: Once the Jingle session exists, participants use the SXE payload defined in XEP-0284: an <sxe/> element in the namespace urn:xmpp:sxe:0, carried in a <message/>, with REQUIRED session and id attributes.

section2.p: To join a session, an entity sends an SXE <connect/> element to the host.

The host (or the initiator) offers the current document state with <state-offer/>. The offer MUST contain the same <description/> element that was used in the Jingle session-initiate, so that the joiner can verify the application type.
The joiner accepts one offer with <accept-state/> and refuses unwanted offers with <refuse-state/>.

The state is sent inside a <state/> element bracketed by <document-begin/> and <document-end/>. The prolog attribute of <document-begin/> carries the XML prolog (including the DOCTYPE) as a data: URI.

example.caption: Sending the state of a new, empty whiteboard

section2.example: <message from='kingclaudius@shakespeare.lit/castle' to='laertes@shakespeare.lit/castle'> <sxe xmlns='urn:xmpp:sxe:0' session='851ba2' id='b'> <state> <document-begin prolog='data:text/xml,%3C%3Fxml%20version%3D%271.0%27%3F%3E%0A%3C%21DOCTYPE%20svg%20PUBLIC%20%27-%2F%2FW3C%2F%2FDTD%20SVG%201.1%2F%2FEN%27%20%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2FGraphics%2FSVG%2F1.1%2FDTS%2Fsvg11.dtd%27%3E'/> <new rid='0' type='element' ns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' name='svg' primary-weight='0'/> <new rid='1' type='attr' name='version' chdata='1.2' parent='0'/> <new rid='2' type='attr' name='baseProfile' chdata='tiny' parent='0'/> <new rid='3' type='attr' name='viewBox' chdata='0 0 600 400' parent='0'/> <document-end last-sender='' last-id=''/> </state> </sxe> </message>

section1.p: All edits are SXE edits inside a <state/> element (XEP-0284). The three edit elements are:

ul.li: <new/> — create a record (attributes rid, type, parent, primary-weight, ns, name, chdata, and optionally version).
<set/> — change a record (attributes target, version, and the field or fields being changed, including parent, primary-weight, name, chdata, replacefrom, replacen).

section1.p: Ordering among siblings is determined by primary-weight and, on ties, by the secondary weight (RID comparison) as defined in XEP-0284. The following examples use the root RID 0 from Section 7.3.

section2.p: Freehand drawing creates a <path/> element and its attributes. Every element that can be selected, transformed, reordered, grouped or deleted SHOULD carry a unique id attribute.
section2.example: <sxe xmlns='urn:xmpp:sxe:0' session='851ba2' id='8'> <state> <new rid='8' type='element' name='path' parent='0' primary-weight='1'/> <new rid='9' type='attr' name='id' chdata='e1f2a3b4' parent='8'/> <new rid='10' type='attr' name='d' chdata='M 100 100 L 300 100 L 200 300 Z' parent='8'/> <new rid='11' type='attr' name='stroke' chdata='#ff0000' parent='8'/> <new rid='12' type='attr' name='stroke-width' chdata='2' parent='8'/> <new rid='13' type='attr' name='fill' chdata='none' parent='8'/> </state> </sxe>
section2.p: Implementations MAY smooth freehand input by emitting SVG curve commands (Q, C) in the d attribute.
Transformations are represented by the SVG transform attribute. There is no separate move command: moving, rotating or scaling updates the attribute record with a <set/>.

example.caption: Moving the path by 100 pixels down and to the right

section2.example: <sxe xmlns='urn:xmpp:sxe:0' session='851ba2' id='9'> <state> <new rid='14' type='attr' name='transform' chdata='matrix(1 0 0 1 100 100)' parent='8'/> </state> </sxe>
<sxe xmlns='urn:xmpp:sxe:0' session='851ba2' id='10'> <state> <set target='14' version='1' chdata='matrix(0.707 0.707 -0.707 0.707 100 100)'/> </state> </sxe>

example.caption: Recolouring the path and thickening its stroke

section2.example: <sxe xmlns='urn:xmpp:sxe:0' session='851ba2' id='11'> <state> <set target='11' version='1' chdata='#0000ff'/> <set target='12' version='1' chdata='6'/> </state> </sxe>
section2.p: A partial replacement MAY use replacefrom and replacen.
RIDs of removed records MUST NOT be reused within the session.
Grouping creates a <g/> element and reparents the selected records under it by changing their parent field.
section2.example: <sxe xmlns='urn:xmpp:sxe:0' session='851ba2' id='13'> <state> <new rid='30' type='element' name='g' parent='0' primary-weight='5'/> <new rid='31' type='attr' name='id' chdata='e5c7d9e0' parent='30'/> <set target='8' version='1' parent='30'/> <set target='20' version='1' parent='30'/> </state> </sxe>
section2.p: Ungrouping composes the group's transform into each child, moves the children back to the group's parent, and removes the group.

example.caption: Bringing the path to the front

section2.example: <sxe xmlns='urn:xmpp:sxe:0' session='851ba2' id='14'> <state> <set target='8' version='2' primary-weight='9999'/> </state> </sxe>

section2.p: In the minimal profile, image data is embedded as a data: URI in the xlink:href attribute. The XLink namespace is http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink.
section2.example: <sxe xmlns='urn:xmpp:sxe:0' session='851ba2' id='15'> <state> <new rid='40' type='element' name='image' parent='0' primary-weight='6'/> <new rid='41' type='attr' name='x' chdata='120' parent='40'/> <new rid='42' type='attr' name='y' chdata='80' parent='40'/> <new rid='43' type='attr' name='width' chdata='64' parent='40'/> <new rid='44' type='attr' name='height' chdata='64' parent='40'/> <new rid='45' type='attr' ns='http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink' name='xlink:href' chdata='data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUg...' parent='40'/> </state> </sxe>
<sxe xmlns='urn:xmpp:sxe:0' session='851ba2' id='16'> <state> <set target='3' version='1' chdata='0 0 1024 768'/> </state> </sxe>

section2.p: There is no clear command; clearing removes every drawable child of the root <svg/>. Metadata (<title/>, <desc/>, <defs/>) SHOULD be preserved.
section2.example: <sxe xmlns='urn:xmpp:sxe:0' session='851ba2' id='17'> <state> <remove target='8'/> <remove target='20'/> <remove target='40'/> </state> </sxe>

section1.p: A whiteboard MAY be hosted in a Multi-User Chat room (XEP-0045) or a dedicated component. The host is the room's bare JID; SXE payloads are sent as type='groupchat' messages to that JID and are reflected to all occupants. Jingle session management is likewise performed with the room as the peer.
Broadcast presence within the room MAY advertise a session using the SXE presence element defined in XEP-0284:

example.caption: Advertising a whiteboard session in presence

section1.p: When a session is started without a user-supplied document, the initiator MUST initialize it to the empty whiteboard document below.

ul.li: The root element MUST be <svg/> in http://www.w3.org/2000/svg.
The canvas MUST be described by the viewBox attribute.
SVG Tiny 1.2 (or a compatible profile) SHOULD be used; baseProfile='tiny' is RECOMMENDED.
Drawable content consists of SVG elements such as <path/>, <image/>, <g/> and basic shapes.
Metadata (<title/>, <desc/>, <defs/>) MUST NOT be treated as drawable items and SHOULD be preserved.

section1.p: The synchronization vocabulary, the record model and the conflict-handling model are defined by XEP-0284 and are not repeated here. This section defines only the application type and the document profile.

section2.p: The shared document SHOULD conform to the following schema, which restricts it to the primitives used by whiteboards.
section2.code: <?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?> <xs:schema xmlns:xs='http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema' targetNamespace='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' elementFormDefault='qualified'> <xs:element name='svg'> <xs:complexType> <xs:choice minOccurs='0' maxOccurs='unbounded'> <xs:any namespace='##targetNamespace' processContents='lax'/> </xs:choice> <xs:attribute name='version' type='xs:string'/> <xs:attribute name='baseProfile' type='xs:string'/> <xs:attribute name='viewBox' type='xs:string' use='required'/> </xs:complexType> </xs:element> <xs:element name='path'> <xs:complexType> <xs:attribute name='d' type='xs:string' use='required'/> <xs:attributeGroup ref='presentation'/> <xs:attribute name='transform' type='xs:string'/> <xs:attribute name='id' type='xs:ID'/> </xs:complexType> </xs:element> <xs:element name='image'> <xs:complexType> <xs:attribute name='x' type='xs:string' use='required'/> <xs:attribute name='y' type='xs:string' use='required'/> <xs:attribute name='width' type='xs:string' use='required'/> <xs:attribute name='height' type='xs:string' use='required'/> <xs:attribute name='href' type='xs:anyURI' use='required'/> <xs:attribute name='transform' type='xs:string'/> <xs:attribute name='id' type='xs:ID'/> </xs:complexType> </xs:element> <xs:attributeGroup name='presentation'> <xs:attribute name='stroke' type='xs:string'/> <xs:attribute name='stroke-width' type='xs:string'/> <xs:attribute name='stroke-linecap' type='xs:string'/> <xs:attribute name='stroke-linejoin' type='xs:string'/> <xs:attribute name='fill' type='xs:string'/> <xs:attribute name='fill-opacity' type='xs:string'/> <xs:attribute name='stroke-opacity' type='xs:string'/> <xs:attribute name='opacity' type='xs:string'/> </xs:attributeGroup> </xs:schema>

section2.p: The d attribute uses the full SVG path data grammar (from the SVG specification); the supported commands include moveto (M/m), lineto (L/l), horizontal and vertical lineto (H/h, V/v), closepath (Z/z), cubic and smooth cubic curves (C/c, S/s), quadratic and smooth quadratic curves (Q/q, T/t), and elliptical arcs (A/a). The transform attribute uses the SVG transform-list grammar.

ul.li: Embedded data: images can be large; implementations SHOULD enforce size and format limits.
Clients SHOULD render the shared document without fetching external resources.
Any participant may edit the document; access control is out of scope and may be provided by the host.
The XML prolog carried in the prolog attribute MUST be treated as untrusted input.

section1.p: This document requires no interaction with the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA).
The Registrar is requested to register the application type urn:xmpp:jingle:apps:svg-whiteboard:0 in its registry of Jingle application formats.
section1.code: <application> <name>svg-whiteboard</name> <desc>An SVG document collaboratively edited over Shared XML Editing (XEP-0284).</desc> <transport>sxe</transport> <doc>XEP-XXXX</doc> </application>

section1.p: The extended profile adds optional capabilities on top of the minimal profile. All of them are negotiated through Service Discovery or Entity Capabilities, so a minimal client can participate in the same session without implementing them. The application type namespace is unchanged, and the shared document always remains a complete, self-describing SVG document.

section2.p: Implementations SHOULD use Entity Capabilities (XEP-0115) so that the features listed in Section 6 can be discovered from presence without an explicit disco#info request.

section2.topic: Image References via HTTP File Upload
section2.p: Instead of embedding large images as data: URIs, an implementation MAY advertise HTTP File Upload (XEP-0363) and place the resulting URL in the image's xlink:href attribute. The document remains self-describing and the binary payload is not duplicated in every edit.

example.caption: An image referenced from an uploaded file

section2.example: <sxe xmlns='urn:xmpp:sxe:0' session='851ba2' id='20'> <state> <new rid='40' type='element' name='image' parent='0' primary-weight='6'/> <new rid='41' type='attr' name='x' chdata='120' parent='40'/> <new rid='42' type='attr' name='y' chdata='80' parent='40'/> <new rid='43' type='attr' name='width' chdata='640' parent='40'/> <new rid='44' type='attr' name='height' chdata='480' parent='40'/> <new rid='45' type='attr' ns='http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink' name='xlink:href' chdata='https://upload.shakespeare.lit/file/9f2c1a' parent='40'/> </state> </sxe>
section2.p: Implementations MUST fall back to the inline data: URI of the minimal profile when the peer does not support uploads or when the referenced resource is not reachable.

section2.topic: Large Attachments via Jingle File Transfer
section2.p: For very large images or other binary content, an implementation MAY use Jingle File Transfer (XEP-0234) out of band and then reference the received content in xlink:href, or embed it as a data: URI once received. The choice is local; the shared document always carries a resolvable reference.

An implementation MAY use Jingle Message Initiation (XEP-0353) to propose a whiteboard inside an existing chat, so that the recipient sees a proposal and accepts with a single action instead of a full Jingle negotiation.

ol.li: Determine the peer's features (Entity Capabilities or disco#info).
Start the session only if the peer advertises urn:xmpp:jingle:apps:svg-whiteboard:0 and the SXE transport.
Use HTTP File Upload for images only if the peer advertises urn:xmpp:http:upload:0; otherwise embed the image as a data: URI.
If the peer supports none of the required features, do not start the session.

table.caption: Comparison of the related whiteboarding approaches

section1.p: A client that supported the deprecated Psi profile must be updated to the Jingle-based session management and the urn:xmpp:sxe:0 namespace; the record model and edit elements are otherwise the same as in XEP-0284.

The whiteboard model is derived from the whiteboarding and Shared XML Editing work of Joonas Govenius in the Psi instant messaging client. This profile modernizes that work onto the standardized XEP-0284 framework.
